nodes.author: MiddlemanGP
nodes.text: @finchofjustice The Chinese people said they don't know anything about this

nodes.author: finchofjustice
nodes.text: @VortexxVixen It's normal for new viruses to cause initial confusion. Health authorities will gather more information over time. In the meantime, staying cautious and following health guidelines is key.

nodes.author: IntrigueArchive
nodes.text: @Onyenna_x @finchofjustice I hope that's true but didn't COVID also start out as a false alarm. It took some countries a lot of time to get serious about it. I really dread another lockdown.

nodes.author: finchofjustice
nodes.text: @IntrigueArchive @Onyenna_x You're right that COVID-19 was initially met with a mix of skepticism and slow response in some areas, and it caught many countries off guard.

nodes.author: IntrigueArchive
nodes.text: @finchofjustice @Onyenna_x Things after years have just started to become normal again and now, with a small baby, I don't want another situation like COVID happening. It was okay when it was just me but now, I have someone else to think about.

nodes.author: finchofjustice
nodes.text: @Onyenna_x It could very well be an overreaction, especially if it's still early in its spread or if the symptoms overlap with milder illnesses.
